national.name: Alzheimer's Association 24/7 Helpline
national.description: Free, confidential support any time, day or night, from specialists and master's-level clinicians. Help is available in many languages.

national.name: Alzheimer's Foundation of America
national.description: A helpline staffed by licensed social workers, plus education and programs for families.

national.name: Eldercare Locator
national.description: A public service that connects you with local services for older adults and caregivers, such as meals, transportation, and in-home help.

national.name: Family Caregiver Alliance
national.description: Fact sheets, online support groups, and state-by-state information on services for family caregivers.

national.name: National Institute on Aging: Alzheimer's and Dementia
national.description: Reliable, plain-language information about the disease, caregiving, and research from the U.S. government.

national.name: ARCH National Respite Network
national.description: Help finding respite care, so you can take a break while your loved one is cared for.

national.name: AARP Family Caregiving
national.description: Guides on care planning, finances, and legal matters, and a resource finder for caregivers.

international.name: Alzheimer's Disease International
international.description: The worldwide federation of Alzheimer associations. Use its member list to find the association in your country.

crisis.name: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline (U.S.)
crisis.description: Caregiving can be crushing, and caregivers matter too. If you are feeling hopeless or thinking about suicide, free and confidential support is available 24/7 by phone, text, or chat.
